mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Certificate of Incorporation of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the country of origin; for the Taiwan investor, the Ministry of Economic Affairs Enterprise Administration / company registration authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) if the source jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state, notarize locally and obtain a single Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; (2) if the source is a non-member state other than Taiwan, notarize locally, authenticate through the origin Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and obtain Consular Legalization from the PRC Embassy/Consulate; (3) if the source is Taiwan, use Taiwan notary public notarization, then Straits Exchange Foundation certification, followed by ARATS verification in mainland China. Apostille and consular/channel legalization must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certified current company registration record of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs or competent company registry of the foreign investor's jurisdiction; Taiwan branch corporate filing bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member state: notarized copy plus Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarization, Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, PRC Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: Taiwan notarization with SEF certification and ARATS verification. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and may not be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the establishment of the China WFOE and appointment of legal representative and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign investor; notarized by the notary public of the investor's jurisdiction and authenticated as applicable
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member: notarized resolution plus Apostille from the competent authority; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarize, authenticate through the origin MFA, then PRC Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: Taiwan notary, then SEF certification and ARATS verification. No sequential chaining of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or constitutive charter file of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign investor's corporate secretarial service or company registrar; for Taiwan, the Ministry of Economic Affairs registered articles and notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member: certified copy plus Apostille from designated Competent Authority; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarization, origin MFA authentication, PRC Embassy Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: Taiwan notarial channel, SEF certification, and ARATS verification. These authentication routes may not be used in series.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank or issuing branch of the foreign investor, signed by the authorized bank officer and bearing the corporate banking seal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member: bank-notarized signature plus Apostille; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarize signature, authenticate at the origin MFA, then PRC Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: notarize the letter at a Taiwan notary public, certify through SEF, verify through ARATS. Apostille and consular legalization paths must remain separate and non-sequential.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificated Register of Directors and Shareholders or Incumbency Certificate of the foreign investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate service provider or company registry as maintained under the governing companies law; for Taiwan, certified company registration records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member state: certified copy plus Apostille; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarization, origin MFA authentication, PRC Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: Taiwan notarization, SEF certification, ARATS verification. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternatives and may not be chain-applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Natural Person UBO Declaration with certified passport copy of each 25% or more beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner before a notary public, or certified by professional counsel under AML client due diligence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication path is origin-specific and mutually exclusive: (1) Hague member: notarized declaration and passport copy plus Apostille; (2) non-member state other than Taiwan: notarization, origin MFA authentication, PRC Consular Legalization; (3) Taiwan: Taiwan notarization, SEF certification, ARATS verification. No document may pass through both Apostille and Consular Legalization.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All natural and juridical persons holding 25 percent or more ownership, all directors, legal representatives, authorized signatories, and actual business controllers of the WFOE must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Consolidated Non-SDN Lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, PBOC watchlists, SAMR registration blacklists, and the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctioned persons list. PEP checks must cover foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, immediate family members, close associates, and persons acting on behalf of a PEP; any PEP nexus or sanctions match triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, negative-media review, and periodic transaction monitoring, all documented in the AML/CFT client file before incorporation and refreshed semiannually.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Registration System under the State Administration for Market Regulation, accessible through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the National Integrated Government Online Service Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE name must be composed exclusively of simplified Chinese characters, and a transliterated Chinese trade name derived from the foreign investor's legal name is required where the investor uses a non-Chinese script. The statutory four-tier naming structure is: administrative division prefix, distinctive trade name selected by the investor, industry or business characteristic phrase, and legal form suffix. Foreign letters, Arabic numerals, or phonetic pinyin may appear only with special registration approval in designated high-technology zones; the primary name must be fully valid Chinese. The registered Chinese name must correspond consistently on the company seal, bank account, tax registration, and invoice.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant must obtain the written refusal reason and application reference number from the SAMR name clearance portal. Within 15 working days, or such shorter period stated in the refusal notice, the applicant must submit a formal Name Reconsideration Application to the local Market Regulation Bureau that issued the rejection, annexing the proposed name, registration application ID, foreign investor certificate of incorporation, trademark certificates, and a legal memorandum explaining the permissibility of the trade name. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file administrative reconsideration with the next higher SAMR administration within 60 days, and may subsequently initiate administrative litigation in the competent People's Court. For sensitive tokens requiring ministerial approval, counsel should file a waiver application with SAMR and maintain an auditable appeal trail; after exhausting the statutory window, a fresh name reservation may be filed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding-only address is rejected by PRC tax authorities and major commercial banks as the registered office of a WFOE engaged in the ISIC 6202 offshore software development center business because the company registry requires a lawful and verifiable operating address and tax registration presupposes proof of actual business premises. In government-sanctioned pilot Free Trade Zones, a nested address or sublease seat leased from an officially authorized incubator or zone administrator may be accepted for registration, but a physical presence with employees, equipment, and records is still required for a credible bank KYC profile. Banks will decline account onboarding if the address is an unqualified virtual office, and the State Taxation Administration may reclassify the taxpayer as having low commercial substance on-site. The prudent structure is a fully leased physical office with payroll, computing infrastructure, and management oversight.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced and announced on-site inspections: (1) registered office signboard matching the SAMR-registered Chinese company name; (2) long-term lease agreement rather than a virtual desk; (3) rent invoices and paid bank transfers; (4) utility invoices in the company name; (5) on-site employees consistent with payroll; (6) hardware, software licenses, and source repository activity evidencing offshore development operations; (7) statutory books, seals, board minutes, and bank records kept at the address; (8) evidence of actual day-to-day management. Quantified risk for an active technology WFOE with genuine physical staffing is low: approximately 5 to 10 percent annual probability of inspection. A taxpayer using a mailbox, shared-desk, or incubator-only address faces a 25 to 40 percent chance of a tele-check or physical visit and a 60 percent or greater likelihood of bank account onboarding refusal.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 1, 128-131, 153-156 and 172; Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 6-7; Company Registration Standards (公司登記辦法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commercial Affairs, via the Company and Commerce Registration One-Stop Online Portal (公司與商業一站式申請作業).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (公司章程) and Company Registration Application Form (公司登記申請書) submitted through the MOEA online system.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for information technology services; a paid-up capital of at least NTD 500,000 (approximately USD 16,000) is recommended to satisfy banking and foreign investment review, with funds deposited in a temporary escrow account pending issuance of the capital certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the foreign sole shareholder subscribes to 500,000 ordinary shares of NTD 1 each, paid in full from the escrow account; that the registered office is established at the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation; that [Name] is appointed Director and General Manager and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary; that these officers are authorized to execute incorporation filings, lease agreements, bank arrangements and business licensing; and that all acts of the incorporators prior to this resolution are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Foreign Investment Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA Department of Commercial Affairs and Investment Commission (Investment Commission), Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit proposed company name and business scope through the MOEA one-stop portal for name pre-approval; concurrently file a foreign investor application with the Investment Commission, including a notarized certificate of incorporation from the parent company and a plan describing the offshore software development activities.
required_dossiers: Notarized copy of parent company incorporation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, resubmit with an alternative name. For the investment application, respond to MOEA comments within 14 days or request an extension via the online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrow Account and Deposit of Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed commercial bank in Taiwan (local bank with foreign exchange dealings)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the company name, deposit the initial paid-up capital, and obtain a bank certificate of deposit and proof that funds remain unwithdrawn pending registration.
required_dossiers: Bank application for foreign currency remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide the bank with a dividend or capital remittance affidavit if required. If the bank delays, request a written refusal and escalate to the Foreign Exchange Department of the Central Bank of China (Taiwan).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public (公證人) or local district court notary office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Have the shareholders' articles of incorporation prepared in Chinese, including capital structure, registered office, director appointment, and business scope. Execute and notarize the articles before a licensed notary; the notarized document is a prerequisite for MOEA registration.
required_dossiers: Identity or company passport of the foreign shareholder
Power of attorney for the Taiwanese representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notary queries translation or authentication, provide a certified Chinese translation of the foreign documents and, if necessary, an apostilled copy from the jurisdiction of the parent company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Registration to MOEA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs (Central Registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the company registration application with the notarized articles, capital certificate, statutory officer declarations, and registered office consent through the one-stop portal. Pay the registration fee online and electronically sign with the representative's MOEA-issued certificate.
required_dossiers: Consent of the registered office owner
Directors' and secretary's Statement of Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA issues a defect notice, rectify within 14 days by amending the deficiency in the online portal and resubmitting supporting documents. If the matter contests a legal point, request formal administrative review or appeal to the Administrative Appeals Commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and National Health/Labor Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (branch of the jurisdiction) and Ministry of Labor (Labor Insurance and Health Insurance Systems)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the company registration certificate, apply to the regional National Taxation Bureau for a unified business tax number and VAT registration ( taxable business certificate). Register the company as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and National Health Insurance Administration and submit the employment rules for the first staff hires.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement of the registered office
Bank account certificate in company name
List of initial employees and authorized HR representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, request an expedited walk-in appointment at the branch tax office. For labor registration, clarify any inaccuracies in employee data immediately through the online employment insurance portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Office Premises Physical and Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal/Metropolitan Government Department of Urban Development and Fire Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a building occupancy permit (使用執照) that authorizes the office to be used for software development operations. Obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local Fire Department or an appointed fire safety management specialist; install devices required by fire safety regulations, including extinguishers, emergency lighting and exit signage.
required_dossiers: Lease contract or property ownership certificate
Civil defense safety plan for workplace evacuation
Report of the building structural load assessment (if floors are added with hardware)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the fire inspection results in non-compliance, complete remedial measures within the statutory abatement order period and request a re-inspection. Appeal any questionable enforcement of structural requirements to the municipal Construction Management Office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6202 software development; the relevant oversight is the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, supplemented by the municipal Department of Urban Development for office building occupancy.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Registration Certificate (營業登記證) and Office Occupancy Permit (使用執照) - no special industrial operating permit is required for offshore software engineering centers.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan (via local environmental protection bureau)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category D (no EIA report or registration required for IT service offices that do not carry out physical manufacturing, chemical use, or wastewater discharge).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with general commercial waste separation under the Waste Disposal Act; wastewater from domestic washrooms and kitchens discharged to municipal sewer in accordance with the Water Pollution Control Act (effluent concentration limits for BOD and suspended solids); no volatile organic compound (VOC) exhaust points are permitted in a software office.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Fire Department under the Fire Services Act, confirming the installation of detectors, extinguishers and exit signage; structural load inspection record for any raised floors or server rooms; and occupational safety clearance in accordance with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including ergonomic workstations, electrical cord inspection, and first-aid provisions for computer-based work.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Bureau having jurisdiction over the entity's registered office, supported by the Ministry of Economic Affairs company registration system and the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign investor must first establish or register the Taiwan legal vehicle with the Ministry of Economic Affairs or the competent local authority, obtain foreign investment approval where applicable, complete company registration, secure a registered office, and complete business registration with the competent National Taxation Bureau before commencing taxable activities. The authority issues an eight-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號), which functions as the principal tax and business identification number. VAT registration is incorporated into business registration. Required materials generally include the approved company or branch registration documents, articles of incorporation, registered-agent and office information, responsible person's identification, foreign investor and ownership documents, capital verification or remittance evidence where required, business-scope information, and power of attorney for local filing. Additional registration may be required for employees, withholding tax, customs, import-export operations, and electronic invoices. The submitted entity profile is internally inconsistent: Taiwan does not use the Mainland China Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise legal form. A Taiwan subsidiary should ordinarily be registered as a company limited by shares or a company limited by guarantee or shares under Taiwan law, while a foreign company branch is registered as a branch. The Unified Business Number and tax registrations must therefore correspond to the legally approved Taiwan form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan generally taxes companies as separate legal persons and does not provide a United States-style check-the-box election. A Taiwan company is subject to Taiwan corporate income tax on Taiwan-source income and, subject to applicable rules, offshore income under the alternative minimum tax regime. A foreign company branch is taxed on Taiwan-source income attributable to the branch. Partnerships and certain other transparent arrangements may receive flow-through treatment under their specific statutory rules, but a limited-liability company or subsidiary cannot elect ordinary pass-through treatment merely by filing a tax classification election. Taiwan's transfer-pricing, controlled foreign company, permanent establishment, and anti-avoidance rules may apply irrespective of the entity's accounting classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added Business Tax (VAT-type business tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Ordinary businesses must generally complete business and VAT registration before commencing business; there is no general turnover threshold that permits an ordinary taxable company to operate without registration. Small businesses and certain exempt operators may be subject to special assessment or exemption rules, commonly associated with monthly sales thresholds of approximately NT$100,000 for goods and NT$50,000 for services, subject to statutory classification and current administrative rules. A software engineering and maintenance company should not assume that these small-business thresholds apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan's electronic invoice system is administered through the Ministry of Finance platform and approved software or service providers. VAT-registered businesses must issue government-compliant Uniform Invoices, with electronic invoicing required or phased in for specified taxpayers and transaction types. Electronic invoices generally require transmission to the Ministry of Finance electronic invoice platform within the prescribed reporting period, including buyer, seller, transaction amount, tax, invoice, and carrier information. Taiwan does not generally operate a universal real-time pre-clearance model equivalent to Brazil's NF-e or Italy's SDI for every invoice. Digital signatures, approved formats, platform transmission, retention, cancellation, allowance, and credit-note controls must follow Ministry of Finance requirements. Customs-linked electronic declarations apply separately to imports and exports.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% business-tax rate may apply to exported goods, goods supplied to export enterprises for export in qualifying circumstances, services supplied to foreign customers and used outside Taiwan, international transportation, and other categories expressly recognized under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act and its regulations. For an offshore development center, 0% treatment for software development, maintenance, support, or other services requires evidence that the contractual customer is outside Taiwan, the services are supplied to and used by the foreign customer outside Taiwan, the transaction is properly invoiced, consideration is received through an acceptable payment channel, and the services are not effectively consumed or performed for a Taiwan domestic customer. Service location, deliverables, personnel activity, contractual terms, payment records, and customer status are critical. Domestic use, Taiwan-based beneficiaries, or insufficient evidence may result in reclassification at 5%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration and export release record for exported goods, where applicable
Commercial invoice, packing list, and transport document such as bill of lading, air waybill, or equivalent, where applicable
Service agreement, statement of work, purchase order, and deliverable or acceptance records for exported software and offshore services
Evidence identifying the foreign customer and confirming offshore use of the services
Uniform Invoice or approved electronic invoice showing the applicable zero-rated treatment
Bank remittance advice, foreign-exchange settlement record, or other acceptable payment evidence linking the proceeds to the invoiced export transaction
Foreign-currency account records and reconciliation between invoices, contracts, receipts, and VAT returns
Subcontractor, timesheet, system-log, deployment, and project-location evidence where required to substantiate offshore performance and use
Import and export permits, technical-control documents, and customs records where the transaction involves controlled software, equipment, or regulated goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan does not impose a universal 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for every export service or zero-rated transaction. The 180-day value should therefore be treated as a compliance-control deadline for collection, documentation, and exception escalation unless a specific financing, banking, customs, investment, or regulatory rule applies. Export zero-rating may be denied or reversed if the transaction lacks proof of export, foreign customer status, offshore use, payment, or proper invoicing. The taxpayer may be assessed the underpaid 5% business tax, interest, surcharges, and applicable penalties, with corresponding denial or clawback of input-tax credits or refunds. False invoices, fabricated export evidence, concealment, or other tax evasion may trigger administrative fines and criminal liability under Taiwan tax and criminal laws. Customs violations may result in additional customs penalties, forfeiture, and investigation. Refund claims are subject to documentary review, audit, post-refund examination, repayment, interest, and penalties where the zero-rating conditions were not satisfied.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a bifurcated convertibility regime. Current account items (software service exports, import of goods, travel, dividends remitted from lawfully accumulated profits) are de facto freely convertible upon bona fide documentary verification under SAFE Circular 28/2013 (Sale of Foreign Exchange for Current Account). Capital account items—including foreign direct investment (share capital injection), external debt, and outbound investment—remain subject to mandatory registration, approval, or filing with SAFE and/or the National Development and Reform Commission and the Ministry of Commerce. Profit remittance for a WFOE requires: (i) audited financial statements, (ii) evidence of corporate income tax final settlement (annual CIT filing, Chinese corporate income tax payment certificate), (iii) shareholders' dividend distribution resolution, and (iv) bank deferential verification of no unpaid statutory reserves (surplus reserve fund must be allocated at 10% of profit until reaching 50% of registered capital). Since the 2015–2019 SAFE reforms, repatriation of bona fide capital is permitted, but the parent must complete FDI Pay-Out Registration and the local bank handles the remittance against the validated dividend documentation. There are no residual quantitative dividend caps, but effective taxation (10% withholding on dividends unless reduced under the PRC–Hong Kong or PRC–Singapore tax treaties, or within the WFOE's own preferential bracket) acts as a de facto remittance cost. Restrictions may intensify under macro-prudential FTZ or capital-flow monitoring windows; treasury should maintain dual-scenario liquidity planning.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The statutory mandatory surrender obligation for export proceeds was formally abolished by SAFE's 2012 reform (implemented in SAFE Circular 2/2019 and Banking Guidance). Exporters are no longer required to convert foreign currency into RMB at a fixed ratio or within a statutory eight-day surrender window. However, all export proceeds must be repatriated into a domestic settlement foreign-exchange account (出口收入待核查账户 concept ceased, replaced by direct settlement account) within the legally permitted 'reasonable period'—interpreted administratively as proceeds should normally arrive within 180 days of the customs clearance date for goods trade; for service trade (software/ODC), the 'deemed receipt' standard is 90 days from service completion absent a contractual deferral. Proceeds may be retained indefinitely in a foreign-currency account at a designated bank, but banks must report to SAFE via the Foreign Exchange Monitoring System (as-verified settlement). The enterprise is free to sell the currency at market rates; however, SAFE applies the 'converted use' verification doctrine: retained foreign currency may only be used for approved current or capital expenditures, and any cross-border outflow requires matching underlying documentation. For software service exporters (ISIC 6202), each inbound SWIFT receipt must be matched to a 'Service Trade Foreign Exchange Payment/Receipt' transaction in the bank system, supported by a service contract, commercial invoice, delivery acceptance certificate, and proof of technology/software export type (online transmission or physical media), with payment exceeding USD 50,000 triggering the enhanced verification scale.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Overall feasibility rating: Medium-Low for direct CNY settlement; High as an auxiliary collection rail. Wise (TransferWise Ltd) is an EU-licensed EMI but does not hold a Chinese cross-border payment license and cannot open a Mainland Chinese CNY domestic account; it may only be used for inbound foreign-currency collection (USD/EUR) into a dedicated pass-through account held with a licensed Chinese bank partner (e.g., Citibank China or Bank of Shanghai joint-service model). Payoneer holds a State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) entity and operates via a licensed cross-border payment institution (Currencycloud or China UnionPay partner), but its China service is restricted to collection of e-commerce or freelance proceeds; a software ODC invoicing B2B services to offshore parents would face strict scope limitations because Payoneer's Chinese MPI partners impose a cap of USD 50,000 per aggregate receipt and require underlying e-commerce screen evidence—inadequate for a professional services WFOE. Legal constraint: under the 2021 'Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Cross-Border Payment Institutions' (PBOC), all cross-border RMB/foreign-currency settlement must be routed through banks or PBOC-opinionated licensed payment institutions; non-licensed EMIs cannot directly execute settlement in China. Therefore Wise/Payoneer should be used only as sub-aggregation for incidental small-volume transactions; the primary treasury rail must remain a domestic commercial bank SWIFT account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of the legal representative (法定代表人) or the sole director is de facto mandatory for most Tier-1 banks under the PBOC 'Double Verification' (双人核实) rule on first account opening. The legal representative must appear in person at the bank counter or via a remotely witnessed high-definition video interview with a bank officer, supplemented by face-recognition biometric verification. If the legal representative is a non-resident (Taiwan/offshore parent representative), banks accept the following alternatives: (i) the legal representative appears in person with a valid Taiwan Compatriot Permit (台胞证) or passport, (ii) a local authorized manager (e.g., the WFOE general manager) appears with a notarized Power of Attorney (POA) issued by the legal representative and certified by a PRC notary or the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office, or (iii) a bank officer conducts a home-country physical verification (site visit) at the Taiwan parent office under the institution's 'Expedited Account Opening for Foreign Shareholders' protocol—this is available at BOC and CMB but subject to a 10-business-day review. Remote video-only account opening without any physical meeting is NOT accepted by Tier-1 Chinese commercial banks for corporate accounts; only city commercial banks and digital banks (e.g., WeBank SME, MYbank—prohibited here because they require sole natural-person shareholders) offer full-remote, and they are ineligible for a WFOE. Minimum on-shore processing timeline with full documentation: 7 to 15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder is a Taiwan holding company or BVI/offshore entity—PBOC 'Sanctioned and High-Risk Jurisdiction' red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum/Articles of Association of the Taiwan parent and each intermediate offshore entity; (2) Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration on PBOC Form A covering >25% natural persons, with passport/TAI Compatriot Permit copies; (3) Three-year audited financial statements of parent proving substantive operations and source of wealth; (4) Notarized explainer letter on commercial rationale (ODC labor arbitrage); (5) Proof that no entity in the chain appears on UN, EU, UK, OFAC, or PRC sanctions lists; (6) Taiwan parent's bank reference letter from a reputable Taiwan bank (Chinatrust, Cathay United, or Fubon) issued within 3 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outbound/inbound service trade flows with intra-group counterparties (parent-company service payments)—'Transfer Pricing & Circular Flow' AML overhang
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Cost-plus transfer pricing documentation (TPD) compliant with PRC State Administration of Taxation Bulletin 16/2017, including a full functional analysis and interquartile arm's-length benchmarking of the ODC profit margin; (2) Signed intra-group software development master agreement and each statement-of-work; (3) Delivery evidence (git repository reports, JIRA/Defect tracking cycle, UAT sign-offs) matched to the invoiced scope; (4) SAFE Service Trade Verification Form showing transaction code '228020' (Software Development, Implementation and Maintenance); (5) Full bank statements of WFOE proving no un-cleared dormant balance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid surge in inbound capital (capital injection exceeding RMB 10 million in one calendar quarter) without prior FDI registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) FDI registration certificate issued by SAFE/State Administration for Market Regulation (FDI Quasi-Asset License); (2) Board resolutions of both parent and WFOE approving the capital increase with bank funding schedule; (3) Share transfer or contribution contract authenticated by a PRC notary; (4) Declaration of currency of contribution (USD/RMB) and utilization plan; (5) Undertaking not to circumvent the 'negative list' under the 2020 Foreign Investment Law; (6) Updated Articles of Association filed with SAMR.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Account opening by a Taiwanese or foreign legal representative without PRC social-security/visa evidence—immigration/tax resident mismatch flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Valid work residence permit (外国人工作许可证 or 台港澳人员就业证/exempt scenario under statutory ODC foreign-director allowance), or (2) sufficient evidence of non-work nature: Board resolution appointing a local Chinese general manager with actual operational control; (3) Tax circular showing withholding tax filings on director fees; (4) Hotel/residence proof and entry stamps; (5) Written explanation that the foreign legal representative holds only a non-executive oversight role and a local senior manager will sign the account mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial bank internal policy flag for 'Section 311/China Cross-Border IT Services' if entity invoices for intangible software services—possible IP export review
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Technical classification certificate (软件产品登记 or IT assessment) demonstrating the WFOE performs R&D and not mere royalty collection; (2) Export software contract with the parent expressly stating deliverables pass limitations, no source-code IP assignment outside China, and title remains with WFOE unless transferred per PRC Technology Import/Export regulations; (3) CIT withholding clearance (clearance letter) on any bundled royalties; (4) Integrity pledge that service fees do not embed disguised dividend or royalty components; (5) IT inventory—servers physically located inside China with PBoC/MLPS level-2 filing where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: (1) Setup—parent executes a capital contribution plan and wires USD/EUR from the Taiwan offshore bank (or HK/US intermediary bank) to the WFOE's 'FDI Capital Account' (资本金账户) at a domestic designated bank; the bank requires SAFE FDI Registration Number (previously 'FDI Card') and China's Bank for International Settlement reporting code to accept the credit. (2) Purpose/message code—SWIFT field 23B is CRED; Remittance Information field 70 must state 'INVESTMENT CAPITAL INJECTION FOR SOFTWARE DEVELOPMENT COMPANY [WFOE NAME]—FDI REGISTRATION NO. XXXXX'; banks reject ambiguous descriptions such as 'loan' or 'payment'. (3) Under the 2019 SAFE outsourcing of FDI verification, the bank uses the 'Capital Project Information System' real-time match; funds are credited as restricted-category and cannot be released for working capital until the WFOE files the new FDI ER-Form and, if capital is fully paid and the entity is operational, converts to CNY using a spot transaction. (4) Timing—foreign exchange settlement of the foreign-currency capital account into RMB for operational rents, salary, and tax payments is allowed immediately, but each conversion must be tagged '资本金结汇' in the bank system, with the bank validating that the converted RMB is used for genuine business expenditures within 5 working days. (5) Parent must not inject via a third-party payer—the funding entity on SWIFT must match the registered investor exactly; any intermediary bank charge causes shortfall and requires supplementary injection amendment. (6) If equity injection is staged, each tranche must be evidenced to a capital audit; if postponed beyond the statutory 5-year business term, the bank may freeze un-utilized balance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for the ODC WFOE: (a) SWIFT MT103 direct instruction from the WFOE's domestic bank account to offshore suppliers and vendors (for software licensing renewals, cloud infrastructure (AWS/Google Cloud), contractor sub-payments, and Taiwan-parent administrative sub-chargebacks) executed under current-account 'Service Trade' purpose codes with SAFE verification; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (at-sight / 30–60 days usance) are NOT applicable to software service outflows and should be avoided; rather purchase-order-backed telegraphic transfer (T/T) with enhanced due diligence is used for high-value IT procurement; (c) RMB cross-border clearing through CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) for trade settled in CNY with Hong Kong/Taiwan clearing participants (CTBC/Chinatrust as Taiwan participants); MT103 CNY routing uses the CNAPS CNY settlement code; (d) For outbound dividends, the rail is always SWIFT MT103 from the corporate RMB or FOREIGN-CURRENCY account through the bank to the Taiwan parent via a U.S. dollar correspondent (e.g., Citibank NY, JPM) or directly into a Taiwan NTD account via the bank's Taiwan cross-strait real-time clearing arrangement (银行间跨境人民币清算行 in Taipei—Bank of China Taipei Branch / TBK). Settlement integrity: each outbound > USD 50,000 triggers mandatory bank stamp on the 'Service Trade Exchange Settlement/Receipt Application', ACC comparison, and retention of contract number, tax withholding voucher, and completion evidence; transaction matching to the corresponding MIT/MOT (import/export) forms is not required for services but the WFOE must file an annual SAFE enterprise report via SAMR.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD deliverable Forward Contracts (SHIBOR-based, 1M–12M tenor, available to any current-account-verified WFOE from designated banks)
Cross-currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) qualified under SAFE for a WFOE with both foreign-currency assets and liabilities

Offshore CNH/USD Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDF) executed through the Taiwan parent treasury center at BOCI/HK interbank desks, matched to net CNH exposure (permissible so long as no PRC-funding leakage avoids SAFE verification)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of the competent region, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: File and pay within the first five months after the close of each fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, generally May 1–31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment may trigger tax assessment, interest, and statutory surcharges. A late-payment surcharge generally accrues at 1% per three-day period, subject to a 15% cap; failure to file may result in assessment and additional penalties. No routine administrative strike-off follows solely from a late tax return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner and major-shareholder information report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company Transparency Platform, Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally report during March each year and update reportable information when changes occur, subject to statutory exemptions and current platform rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report or correct information may result in fines under the Company Act, with escalating penalties for continued noncompliance. No automatic strike-off timetable is specified.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and shareholder meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; company registration authority only where a separate filing or registration change is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The board must prepare annual financial statements after fiscal year-end and submit them for shareholder approval at the annual meeting, generally within six months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare or present financial statements may expose responsible directors to Company Act penalties and civil liability. Taiwan generally has no routine annual return or annual financial-statement filing for an ordinary private limited company; registration changes must be filed within the applicable statutory period.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent CPA audit requirements depend on the applicable Company Act and tax rules. Common Company Act triggers include paid-in capital of at least NT$30 million; additional tax-audit triggers may apply based on revenue, assets, industry, or other criteria. Confirm the thresholds and applicable exemptions for the specific company and tax year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan company and tax accounting rules apply. Public companies generally use Taiwan-endorsed IFRS; a private company generally uses applicable Taiwan GAAP or Taiwan-endorsed IFRS, as permitted and selected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Reportable company information is generally confirmed through the annual March reporting process and updated upon relevant changes, subject to exemptions and current Ministry of Economic Affairs rules. This is not a substitute for maintaining accurate shareholding and statutory records.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, where applicable
Articles of Incorporation and shareholder and board meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–2,000 annually; Taiwan companies generally maintain a registered business address rather than appointing a registered agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000–10,000 annually for a small private company; scope, transaction volume, and mandatory audit status materially affect fees.
